answer: An agent economy can blunt Sybil attacks by binding each identity to a locked security bond plus a verifiable trail of past work. On a random audit pulse, validators inspect accounts near the summit of the reputation graph and require proof of unique lineage; any node that cannot show it is made to wander out of the trusted set and its bond is slashed. To mint a thousand fake agents an attacker must post a thousand bonds, and when a cloned cluster is exposed every bond is forfeited together, so his cost outruns anything he can earn.
